method: One core_pattern template is expanded for the sample crash. A leading | makes the value a pipe command line instead of a file name, and the rest is split on white space into a program and its arguments after expansion. Each % is read together with the character that follows it: %% is a literal %, %p and %P are the PID in its own and in the initial PID namespace, %i and %I the triggering thread IDs in those same namespaces, %u and %g the numeric real UID and GID, %h the hostname, %s the signal number, %t the dump time in seconds since the epoch, %d the PR_GET_DUMPABLE mode, %c the soft RLIMIT_CORE in bytes, %C the CPU the task ran on, %e the comm cut to its first 15 bytes, %E the executable path with every slash replaced by !, %f the last segment of that path and %F the pidfd. A % followed by a character core(5) does not list is dropped together with that character, and a single trailing % is dropped, with a row in the table for each. When the template has no %p and the core_uses_pid switch is set, .PID is appended to the name; setting the switch while %p is present is reported as ineffective. Lengths count UTF-8 bytes against the 128-byte maximum core(5) gives a resulting name or a pipe command line. The page warns about a pipe whose program is not absolute, a pipe with no program, a relative file name that fs.suid_dumpable=2 would reject, a zero core size limit with a file template, a comm holding a space in a pipe template, and a space before the leading | that makes it literal. Numeric fields are bounded: PID and thread IDs 1 to 2147483647, UID and GID 0 to 4294967294, signals 1 to 64, CPUs 0 to 8191 and the dump time 0 to 253402300799, while the core limit takes up to 18446744073709551615 as digits without floating point. The pipe marker is shown as not part of the command line, the handler arguments are listed one per line, and the page only expands text: it reads no files, writes no sysctl and makes no network request.

sources.title: core(5): a leading | pipes the dump to a program, %c %C %d %e %E %f %F %g %h %i %I %p %P %s %t %u are the template parameters, a % before any other character is dropped with it, .PID is appended when core_uses_pid is set and %p is absent, and the resulting name is limited to 128 bytes.

Documentation for /proc/sys/kernel/: core_pattern is the core dump file name template, its default value is core, the file holds at most 127 characters, and .PID is appended for backward compatibility when the template omits %p and core_uses_pid is set.
coredumpctl(1): the tool retrieves and processes core dumps and metadata saved by systemd-coredump(8), which is why a systemd host usually never uses the kernel's own file naming.
